title: Zakat institutions
hookLine: mosques and charities collect and distribute zakat today

lines: A TABLE BY THE MOSQUE DOOR.
cards: In the last days of Ramadan, a table goes up near a mosque door: a box, a card reader, a QR code on the wall, a volunteer with a sheet of numbers.
Elsewhere, a charity's website has a zakat calculator and a page saying where last year's money went. The person paying and the family receiving never meet. So who carries the gift across?
The Qur'an's own list of who receives zakat has an answer: the people who collect it.

teach.b: First, the collectors are in the text. Surah nine, verse sixty, lists the eight groups zakat may go to, and among them, in Pickthall's words, "those who collect them."
Collecting and handing out zakat is work, and the Qur'an makes room to pay those who do it from zakat itself. Second, it was a task given to the Prophet himself.
In surah nine, verse one hundred three, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is told: "Take alms of their wealth, wherewith thou mayst purify them and mayst make them grow."

teach.h: TAKEN FROM THE RICH, GIVEN TO THE POOR.
teach.b: When he sent Mu'adh ibn Jabal to Yemen, the report in Sahih al-Bukhari says he told him to teach that zakat is taken from their rich and given back to their poor.
Their rich, their poor: some scholars read that as keeping zakat close to where it was collected.
Third, today the hands differ from country to country: a government agency, a local mosque, a community fund, a charity working across borders.
Scholars discuss the questions these bodies face: whether zakat can go to a poor family far away when there's need nearby, and how much can pay running costs.
Schools and scholars answer differently, and a good zakat charity will tell you which scholars it follows. Fourth, the giver's part.
Giving through an institution isn't less personal; it can reach someone you'd never find alone.
But the giver still asks where it goes, and trusts the hands it passes through.

teach.h: TAKE ALMS OF THEIR WEALTH, WHEREWITH THOU MAYST PURIFY THEM.
teach.b: That closes these days on zakat: a chain of people carrying a right to the one it belongs to.

how: Muslims pay zakat directly to people in need or through mosques, community funds, charities and, in some countries, government zakat agencies, which collect it and distribute it to the eight groups named in the Qur'an.

o: government offices that set a new zakat rate every year
the mosques, funds and charities that carry zakat to the poor
councils of scholars who decide who counts as poor

games.q: zakat through many hands — tap the pairs.
p: take alms, to purify and make grow

s: the Qur'an says nothing about the people who collect zakat
9:60 names "those who collect them" among the eight groups.
the report about Mu'adh says zakat is taken from a people's rich and given to their poor
Sahih al-Bukhari: taken from their rich and given back to their poor.
every scholar gives the same answer on sending zakat far away
schools and scholars answer differently; a good zakat charity says whom it follows.

games.q: a volunteer spends the last nights of Ramadan at the mosque table, collecting zakat and handing it out. can zakat itself pay for that work?
o: no; every coin must go straight to the poor.
yes; 9:60 names those who collect it among the eight.
only if the volunteer is poor too.
games.why: yes. "those who collect them" are one of the eight groups in 9:60, so the work of carrying zakat can be paid from it.

practice: Think of a place where help is needed that you care about: your own city, a place in the news, the place your family comes from.

Hold it for a minute, then picture the hands that would carry a gift there, and the three things you'd want to know about them: who they serve, which scholars they follow, and what share goes to running costs.
You don't have to give anything to do this.

wordCard.voice: Zakat institutions. The mosques, funds, agencies and charities that collect zakat and carry it to the people it belongs to; the Qur'an names the collectors among the eight. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic, Qur'an 9:60: those who work on it, the collectors of zakat, named among its eight recipients.
